newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe bullish on California's crude oils.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe bullish on California's crude oils.

text.p: When Monterey Resources goes public next month on the New York Stock Exchange, the California oil producer will be trying to sell a story of recovery in its long-dormant market.

Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc, the parent company of Monterey, plans to sell 15 percent of the unit's shares in a November public offering on the NYSE as part of a plan to refocus its energy operations.

Santa Fe says prices for California crudes will be priced at 75 to 80 percent of the value of the Alaska North Slope (ANS), the premier West Coast grade which has averaged a 40 to 50 percent premium to California grades, such as Kern River.
"(That) disparity came about because California was awash in crude oil," said Hall.

Surplus still exists, as evidenced by a fall in relative values this year following a stronger 1995 showing. But that weakness followed a build up of inventory this spring when a half-dozen California refineries shut unexpectedly for repairs.
"This is not normal," one West Coast trader said.
Long-term, surplus should wane as exports of ANS begin after a 20-year ban and consumption increases with California's improving economy.
Key heavy grades such as Kern River are now priced at $16.25 a barrel, versus an average of $12.50 over the last five years.

Traders said the December start-up of a coker -- which processes heavy crudes -- at Shell Oil Co's San Francisco refinery will add to demand for heavy crude, which is produced at a rate of 500,000 barrels-per-day in the state.
The new unit also means Shell will stop supplying Unocal Corp with heavy crude from the plant next month. Thereafter, Unocal will be in the market for 35,000 bpd of heavy crude.
"If refineries run right, I think you'll see a much tighter demand/supply situation on heavy," one refiner said.
If that recovery does come about, other California independents and majors active in the region, like Texaco Inc and Shell, also are poised to reap the rewards.
